lines.text: Shah Jahan was fond of arts and architecture. Some of
the most beautiful buildings of the Mughal period were
built during his time such as the Red Fort, Taj Mahal and
the tomb of his wife; Mumtaz Mahel. Shah Jahan
created a wonderful blend of Persian and Indian culture
Shah Jahan built a new capital, Shahjahanabad, with its magnificent Red Fort. In
the Hall of Public Audience, Shah Jahan sat on the Peacock Throne, which
consisted entirely of jewels and precious metals and stones. Four legs of gold
supported the seat;12 pillars ofemeralds heldup the emerald canopy,each pillar
bore two peacocks encrusted with gems and between each pair of peacocks rose
a tree covered with diamonds, emeralds, rubies, and pearls.
